phase: Phase 10: Full Evaluation, Ablation Studies, and Sensitivity Analysis

experimental_matrix_spec.client_heterogeneity: 10 distinct task_load, mobility, and link_reliability distributions (Non-IID)

invariants_verified.task_partition_identity: 100% of 540 core runs satisfy completion_rate + failure_rate + miss_rate == 1.0000
invariants_verified.ground_truth_isolation: Detector inputs strictly derived from behavioural and model metrics, never scenario ground-truth labels
invariants_verified.reproducibility: All random seeds explicitly controlled across NumPy, PyTorch, and Python random generators

free_riding_mitigation.finding: At f=0.40 over 8 FL rounds, zero-update free-riding causes significant degradation in FedAvg (completion drops to 76.5%), whereas Trust-Threshold maintains 80.0% completion with F1=0.982 (precision=0.981, recall=1.000).
free_riding_mitigation.evidence: Observed across 10 random seeds (p < 0.05 vs FedAvg).

copy_update_mitigation.finding: Pairwise cosine duplicate detector maintains 100% recall across all fractions (f=0.1 to 0.4), with F1 increasing from 0.567 to 0.848.
copy_update_mitigation.evidence: Zero duplicate attacks escaped detection across 10 seeds.

honest_non_iid_fpr.finding: Under 10 random seeds and 8 rounds (800 client decisions per strategy), 52 false exclusions were observed, yielding a micro FPR of 6.50% and macro per-run FPR of 6.50% +/- 3.57% (95% CI: [3.95%, 9.05%]).
honest_non_iid_fpr.scientific_implication: Disproves claims of a guaranteed <5% FPR bound under extended training horizons with severe gradient heterogeneity; highlights the essential trade-off between poisoning sensitivity and non-IID tolerance.

gaussian_perturbation_stealth.finding: Gaussian random perturbation achieves F1 = 0.000 across all fractions, demonstrating that uncoordinated isotropic noise does not trigger cosine or norm anomaly filters.
gaussian_perturbation_stealth.scientific_implication: Confirmed across 10 seeds; acknowledged as an inherent limitation of distance/direction heuristic detectors in high dimensions.
